prompt: A car travels at $60$ miles per hour. There are $5{,}280$ feet in a mile and $3{,}600$ seconds in an hour. What is the car's speed, in feet per second?
hint: Chain the conversion factors so the unwanted units cancel.

hints.text: Chain the conversion factors so the unwanted units cancel.
$\dfrac{60 \text{ mi}}{1 \text{ hr}} \times \dfrac{5280 \text{ ft}}{1 \text{ mi}} \times \dfrac{1 \text{ hr}}{3600 \text{ s}}$.

learningObjective: Chain unit conversions using dimensional analysis.
explanation: Write each conversion as a fraction arranged so the unwanted unit cancels diagonally.
$\dfrac{60 \text{ mi}}{\text{hr}} \times \dfrac{5280 \text{ ft}}{1 \text{ mi}} \times \dfrac{1 \text{ hr}}{3600 \text{ s}}$: miles cancel, hours cancel, leaving feet per second.

alternativeExplanations.title: Units are a free error check
steps: If the units left standing are not the ones the question asked for, you have flipped a factor.
That check catches the mistake *before* you do any arithmetic, which is when it is cheapest to fix.
Worth memorizing: $60$ mph is exactly $88$ ft/s. It shows up often enough to recognize.
